title: First Lost Day After a Larkspur-Side Wire Return — Closing and Funding Interest Rules
content:
**Schedule note.** For a Closing and Funding returned-wire refund, the first lost day is set from the kind of Larkspur-side return, read from the closing's latest wire return:

| Latest wire return | First lost day | Why |
|---|---|---|
| a settlement agent rejection of a wire whose amount differs from the amount of the wire that funded the loan (Larkspur's wrong amount) | the date the rejected wire went out (the outgoing wire the return names) | the agent could never disburse it |
| a Larkspur recall because a prior-to-funding item was open (a return marked as funding conditions unmet) | the recall date (the date of the return) | the funds were good until Larkspur pulled them back |
| any other return, or no return | no first lost day | |

The wire that funded the loan is the outgoing wire sent on the disbursement date.

## Cases (hypothetical)

- A 351,000.00 wire went out on the 12th and the settlement agent rejected it on the 13th; the loan was funded by a 350,000.00 wire on the 18th. The amounts differ, so the first lost day is the 12th.
- Larkspur recalled a wire on the 14th because a prior-to-funding condition was still open. The first lost day is the 14th.
- The settlement agent rejected a wire of exactly the funding amount: no first lost day.
- The latest return came back because the borrower rescinded: no first lost day.
